name: How does the local Colorado climate affect drywall drying and sanding?

mainEntity.name: How does the local Colorado climate affect drywall drying and sanding?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, indoor humidity levels often drop very low, particularly during heated winter months, which speeds up surface evaporation. While joint compound might appear dry on the outside, thick coats can remain soft underneath. Sanding too early in dry climates can peel semi-cured compound away from the gypsum core. Conversely, basement finishes in Centennial, Parker, or Aurora homes often experience higher moisture and cooler slab temperatures, requiring extra curing time between coats. Verifying that mud is fully cured from surface to substrate ensures an even, durable sand.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dry indoor winter air dries compound surfaces quickly, while cooler basements dry slower. Ensuring mud is fully cured through prevents surface peeling when sanding.
